title: Canonical ordinary-module derived scalar adjunction and comparisons
statement: Let A, B, D be commutative rings in universe r, with unbounded derived module categories in independently chosen localization universes wR, wS, wT [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For f:A→B and g:B→D use the fixed derived scalar restriction U_f and its left adjoint E_f [def-zl-ring-derived-scalar-extension]. Define the canonical adjunction E_f ⊣ U_f by the right-adjoint structure of U_f. For every integer-indexed cochain complex P of A-modules define the representative map E_f(Q_A P)→Q_B(B⊗_A P) as the transpose under this adjunction of the localization of the ordinary extension/restriction unit P→U_f(B⊗_A P), followed by the canonical comparison identifying localization of exact restriction with derived restriction. Define U_g followed by U_f ≅ U_(g∘f) by localizing the ordinary restriction-of-scalars composition isomorphism and using the canonical comparison for composition of exact derived functors. These are specified constructions; no invertibility of the representative map and no K-flatness, flat-term, boundedness or flatness assumption on f or g is part of this definition.
